Project Description: Existing Mine: Produced about 5 million pounds of copper (underground) from 1909 to 1975, inactive since.
Project Description: Status of Project: The developer did not announce activity in 2024.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: Claims within Salmon National Forest

Location: Additional Location Information:Located 10 miles north of town of Kearney (pop 1,741, 2020), 80 miles southeast of Phoenix, Arizona. 
Project Description: Status of Project: The Ray Complex encompasses the Ray Mine and SXEW Plant, the Ray and Hayden Concentrators, the Hayden Smelter, and the Copper Basin Railroad.  The Hayden concentrator is located next to the Hayden smelter about 20 miles from the Ray mine. In 2009 the 9th Circuit, in a split (2-1) decision, blocked a land exchange that was crucial for an expansion of the Ray Mine.  In 2020 BLM under the Trump administration again approved the land exchange.  Meanwhile, the developer is planning to reopen the shutdown Hayden copper smelter, as there are only two operating smelters in the US: the Miami smelter in Arizona and Kennecott smelter in Utah. 
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: The expansion project which required a public land swap was delayed for 26 years, due to litigation and a ten-year NEPA process. 
Land Ownership: Type of Land: The 2020 land exchange: the BLM acquired 7,298 acres of privately owned land; in exchange, the BLM transferred 9,339 acres of public land adjacent to ASARCO’s Ray Mine Complex and Copper Butte properties near Kearny, for mine expansion.
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: Federal appeals court issued a decision in 2010 opposing the land swap at the Ray Mining Complex in Arizona. The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) later approved the land exchange and addressed the court’s environmental concerns through a 2019 rulemaking. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local/Regional -- WildEarth Guardians; National -- Center for Biological Diversity.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 60 miles east of Phoenix, Arizona, near the town of Superior (pop 2,407, 2020) in northern Pinal County.  Superior was founded as a mining town for the Silver King and the later Magma mines; silver was mined at first, and then copper.
Project Description: Status of Project: Developer activity at the site has been delayed by multiple lawsuits but in 2024 the USFS said it plans to re-publish an environmental report before July that will set in motion a land swap between the U.S. government and Rio Tinto, allowing the miner to develop its Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The developer’s new schedule for the delayed mine calls for production to begin by the end of the decade.  
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: Delays have occurred due to litigation over whether the mine would infringe on the religious rights of the Western Apaches, who believe the site is home to the ga'an or Mountain Spirits and has for centuries been the site of ceremonies for the Western Apaches.  The Forest Service, under the Biden administration, delayed approval of the project during the appeals process, citing the need for more consultation with the Western Apaches.  The 9th Circuit Court rejected the suit by the Apache tribe and approved the land swap, which could allow the developer to begin production by 2030.
Commercial Plans: Planned Production Capacity: 25% of America's copper needs- largest copper mine in US.
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: The developer has plans to smelt the copper in Utah
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: In 2014 the U.S Congress approved a land swap, which gave the developer the rights to access a region of land in central Arizona (near Superior, Arizona) called Oak Flat, which was previously withdrawn from development.  Apache Stronghold, a Western Apache group, sued the US Fish and Wildlife Service on the grounds that the land swap violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution as well as tribal land management statute and a US treaty with tribes regarding consultation and governance. In March 2024, Ninth Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals ruled, in a divided 6-5 decision, that a land swap between the federal government and Resolution Copper could move forward despite a request by the Tribe to halt the exchange. The SCOTUS has not yet decided whether to hear an appeal. In 2023 the Arizona Supreme Court vacated a lower court ruling that the state should not have granted a water permit, because the expansion of the existing mine was a new pollutant source that could damage the Queen Creek (desert) river. The US Supreme Court declined to hear the issue on appeal. 
Litigation: Level of Court: The federal district court upheld the land swap, a split panel (2-1) of the 9th Circuit upheld the land swap, and the entire 9th Circuit upheld the land swap 6-5.  The Supreme Court has not yet decided whether to hear an appeal.
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Apache Stronghold; San Carlos Apache Tribe.
Concerned Interest Groups: Environmental Groups: Spearheaded unsuccessful litigation over the developer's wastewater permit.
Concerned Interest Groups: Evidence of Organized Protest(s): 2014, before the land swap, a group calling itself Apache Stronghold formed to resist the project. It held regular ceremonies to consolidate opposition and focus attention on the imminent threat. In February 2024, the group organized a fifty-mile march to Oak Flat across mountainous terrain, beginning east of the mine site, on the San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation. The march passed through the mining towns of Miami and Globe, ending in the oak and manzanita known as Chi’Chil’Ba’Goteel to the Apache. Dozens made the journey and were met by hundreds more at Oak Flat.
Reasons for Concern: Site of Historical, Cultural, Spiritual Significance: Oak flat is site of Apache religious ceremonies, and past battle between US & Apache tribe. 
Reason for Concern: Classification of Species Impacted: Endangered jaguar and Gila top minnows, threatened Chiricahua leopard frogs.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located approximately 14 miles northeast of Dyer, Nevada. It is 65 miles southwest of Tonopah, Nevada (closest city), 215 miles from Reno (third largest city in Nevada), and 255 miles from Las Vegas (largest city in Nevada). Situated in the Silver Peak Range, part of the Basin and Range physiographic province of southwestern Nevada. Esmeralda County, which has no incorporated communities, is the least populated county in the state of Nevada; the county seat is the town of Goldfield.
Project Description: Existing Mine: Although the area has not previously been mined, it has been explored off and on for decades. The earliest known boron exploration activities began in the 1890s. More recent exploration activities occurred in the 1960s, the 1980s, the 1990s, the 2010s, plus there is the recent exploration by the current developer.  
Project Description: Status of Project: The project is fully permitted and construction has begun. The developer projects that active production could occur by 2028, assuming no judicial setbacks.                       
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: A multi-year delay in federal permitting occurred due to concerns that the project could harm the habitat of a rare desert flower (Tiehm's buckwheat). The Fish and Wildlife Service designated 910 acres of critical habitat on lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management in the Rhyolite Ridge area of the Silver Peak Range in Esmeralda County, Nevada, to help conserve the imperiled plant. The developer modified the location of the mine to minimize the Project's risk to the flower while also pledging use of advanced dust-suppression methods to further protect the flower.  
Developer Description: Lead Developer: Ioneer spent about $172 million over eight years (2017-2024) to develop the project. In September 2021, Sibanye-Stillwater entered into an agreement with Ioneer to establish a joint venture company with respect to Rhyolite Ridge. Sibanye-Stillwater may acquire up to a 50% interest in the Joint Venture, with Ioneer maintaining a 50% interest and retaining operational management responsibility for the Joint Venture.
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: The Rhyolite Ridge Project is planned to consist of an open pit lithium and boron mine (referred to as a Quarry in the Water Pollution Control Permit Application), an Overburden Storage Facility (OSF), a processing plant, a Spent Ore Storage Facility (SOSF), and a sulfuric acid plant (SAP). 
Financial Support: Federal Agency: In 2022 the DOE offered a conditional loan of up to $700 million to support the costs of constructing the processing facility. In early 2025 DOE upped the size of the loan to $996 million.
Financial Support: Public Supply Agreement w/ an Automaker or Battery/Component Producer: The developer has signed binding offtake agreements with Ford Motor Company, with Prime Planet Energy and Solutions (a joint venture of Toyota and Panasonic), EcoPro Innovation, and Nevada-based Dragonfly Energy. 
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: Esmeralda County Economic Development Commission. 
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: One lawsuit concerned whether USDA Fish and Wildlife Service should list Tiehm's buckwheat as endangered under the ESA. The second lawsuit, in 2024, challenged BLM's decision to approve the mine, given the ecological risks involved.  
Litigation: Court Rulings Issued: A federal judge ruled in favor of CBD that the USDA Fish and Wildlife Service must rule within 30 days on CBD's petition to list Tiehm's buckwheat as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act. A coalition of more than 100 scientists and botany groups had urged US F&W Service to list Tiehm’s buckwheat as endangered under the ESA.  
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Western Shoshone.
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Center for Biological Diversity. Local/Regional -- Great Basin Resource Watch.
Reasons for Concern: Site of Historical, Cultural, Spiritual Significance: The mine might harm or destroy sites that are sacred to the Western Shoshone people, such as Cave Spring.
Reasons for Concern: Classification of Species Impacted: In response to a petition from the Center for Biological Diversity, USDA’s Fish and Wildlife Service formally listed Tiehm’s buckwheat, a rare desert flower, as an endangered species, an action that triggered habitat protection measures in the area where the developer proposes to build a lithium mine.

Location: Additional Location Information: Five miles northeast of Noxon (pop 464, 2020), western Montana. Site is located on the Clark Fork River, which flows into Lake Pend Oreille.
Project Description: Status of Project:  The current develper withdrew the Plan of Operations for Rock Creek from consideration by the United States Forest Service (USFS).  This plan was prepared by the project’s prior owner and does not have the data necessary to inform the current developer's plan.  Recently, the current developer decided to give priority to the nearby Montanore project, which made Rock Creek a secondary priority.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: Coalition of tribal and environment groups led by Earthjustice persuaded a state district court judge that the state did not adequately consider the environmental impacts of the project, invalidating the water permit. The Montana Supreme Court ruled 5-2 that the state had adequately considered the environmental impacts.                                  
Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?: June 2015 Hecla acquired the Rock Creek Project through purchase of previous developer Revett Mining Company.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: Officials from nearby counties, including Sanders County, support the project due to the economic development boost.
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: In 2019 a state district court invalidated the developer’s permit to operate based on the allegation of environmental groups that the state had not adequately considered the environmental impacts of the mine.  In 2021 the Montana Supreme Court overruled the district court 5-2, thereby affirming the developer’s permit. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes.
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local/Regional -- Rock Creek Alliance, Clark Fork Coalition, Montana Environmental Information Center; National -- Earthworks, Earthjustice.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located at Round Top Mountain near town of Sierra Blanca (pop 315, 2020) in far west Texas near the Mexican border.  El Paso is approximately 80 miles north-west of the project site.
Project Description: Status of Project: The strategy with Round Top, as revealed in the developer's 2024 SEC filing, is to formulate a metallurgical process to concentrate or extract metals from the Round Top Project’s rhyolite, conduct additional engineering, design, geotechnical work, and permitting necessary for a bankable feasibility study, and then extract mineral resources.
Developer Description: Parent Company: USA Rare Earth is entitled to acquire a 70% interest in the project by spending $10m for the finalization of processing technology and the completion of a bankable feasibility study (BFS). The developer also has an option to acquire an additional 10% interest through a $3m cash payment to TMRC
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: Successful pilot plant in Wheat Ridge, Colorado; plans to move operation to Texas
Land Ownership: Type of Land: Texas General Land Office. The developer holds 19-year renewable leases from the State of Texas on 950 acres encompassing Round Top and additional prospecting permits on adjacent areas covering an additional 9,345 acres.
Statements of Concern from Public Officials: Local: County Commissioner
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local -- Sierra Blanca Legal Defense Fund
Reasons for Concern: Impacts to Natural Environment: Mining method problematic for preserving natural beauty of Round Top Mountain.
Reasons for Concern: Air Quality: Potential emissions of toxic dust, including possible radioactive material.
Reasons for Concern: Historical Mining or Reclamation Issues: Historical fight against hosting landfills for other mining operations; plus residents allege they have too few resources to properly refute claims of mining companies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Reasons for Support: Community Development: The developer’s payments for leasing public land could generate as much as $500 million for use in Texas public schools.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 8 miles from Safford (pop 10,129, 2020), county seat of Graham County, southeast Arizona, 170 miles east of Phoenix.
Project Description: Status of Project: Safford is a mine-for-leach operation that produces copper cathode. The operation consists of three open pits, of which only Lone Star is currently being mined, feeding a crushing facility.  The developer continues to advance plans at Safford/Lone Star to increase volumes to achieve 300 million pounds of copper per year from oxide ores, which reflects expansion of the initial design capacity of 200 million pounds of copper per year. Positive drilling conducted in recent years indicates opportunities to expand production to include sulfide ores in the future. The developer is completing metallurgical testing and mine development planning and expects to commence pre-feasibility studies during 2024-2005 for a potentially significant expansion.
Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?: The mine was established in 1907. Ownership changed hands several times before current developer acquired it.  
Commercial Plans: Planned Production Capacity: 21 million pounds of molybdenum a year as well
Financial Support: Federal Agency: In March 2024 Freeport-McMoRan was selected to receive $80 million through a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of Energy for a project to use geothermal energy to heat leaching stockpiles in Morenci and Safford and integrate battery energy storage and microgrid operations to improve electrical reliability in Morenci. By using geothermal energy, the project aims to generate clean, industrial-scale heat to enable the recovery over time of billions of pounds of residual copper through the company’s Leach to the Last Drop initiative from already mined material previously considered unrecoverable. The project could increase copper recovery by 25 million pounds or more annually, depending on the geothermal resources.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: In September 2005, as part of a land swap, Phelps Dodge (which was subsequently purchased by Freeport-McMoran), transferred 3,867 acres of scattered "environmentally sensitive" land to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and purchased 16,297 acres, located next to where the Safford mine is located, from the BLM. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local -- Sky Island Alliance

Location: Additional Location Information: The nearest town Calipatria (pop 6,515, 2020), is about 23 miles from El Centro (pop 44,432, 2020), which is the county seat of Imperial County in southeastern California; over 100 miles east of San Diego. The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties at the southern end of California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico.
Project Description: Mining Method: The developer will use ILiAD technology (developed by company) to separate lithium into useable form. The technology has been piloted with various brine resources across the United States and internationally, including in Utah, Texas, and Nevada, in addition to onsite in California. 
Project Description: Co-Porducing Materials: The brine features additional recoverable critical minerals supporting America’s industrial base, including zinc and manganese, which ATLiS expects to extract and commercialize.   
Project Description: Status of Project: The Imperial County Planning Commission has approved all aspects of the Project and the developer is working to secure the necessary financial support.  
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: The facility will be sited next to an existing geothermal plant, which will supply the lithium-rich brine from the subsurface geothermal field located over one mile underground. After impurities are removed from the brine, the lithium will be separated out using the ILiAD™ DLE technology. 
Financial Support: Federal Agency: In January 2025, DOE announced a direct loan of up to $1.36 billion to finance the construction, equipping, and operation of the facility in Imperial County, California, to produce lithium hydroxide from geothermal brine. 
Statements of Support from Public Officials: State: Contingent support of Lithium Valley Commission, recognizing need to manage risks. California  Governor Newsome and Congressman Paul Ruiz support the Project. In 2022, California passed a law imposing new taxes on companies engaged in lithium extraction at the Salton Sea. The legislation designates 80% of the generated tax revenue to be distributed among the counties near these plants, with the remaining 20% allocated for the restoration of the Salton Sea. The law has the potential to bring millions in revenue to the historically underfunded region.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Federal: President Biden's domestic-policy advisor Gina McCarthy visited the Salton Sea to endorse the projects. President Biden himself praised the Salton Sea Projects as a strategy to reduce US dependence on China for processed lithium. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Cahuilla Indian Reservation- believe brine to be sacred. Fort Yuma Quechan Tribe- pollution concerns- Faron Owl, tribe member stated concerns over the “Toxic wastes, the gas emissions, the pollution, are being put aside for the lithium demand."
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Earthworks
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: Poses risks to both water quality and quantity in the west due to reliance on already struggling aquifers

Location: Additional Location Information: The nearest town Calipatria (pop 6,515, 2020), is about 23 miles from El Centro (pop 44,432, 2020), which is the county seat of Imperial County in southeastern California; over 100 miles east of San Diego. The developer already has 10 geothermal plants in the Salton Sea region, with a demonstration of lithium extraction in the Imperial Valley at the southern end of the Salton Sea in southeastern California.   The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties at the southern end of California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico.
Project Description: Mining Method: Like other developers applying direct lithium extraction technology in the Salton Sea, this developer has experienced some technical difficulties with corroded equipment from the superhot brine, but technical progress has been made. 
Project Description: Status of Project: In 2024 the California Energy Commission issued its Final Project Report on the developer’s Lithium Recovery Demonstration Project.  The report documented that the Project faced setbacks, leading to the termination of the technology provider's contract due to insufficient progress.  This underscored the significance of brine pretreatment to successful lithium recovery, prompting a shift to alternative technologies focused on enhancing this process. While the Project is considered to be delayed indefinitely, a new joint venture may bring new life to the project.  In June 2024, Occidental and BHE Renewables, a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, announced a joint venture for the demonstration and deployment of TerraLithium’s Direct Lithium Extraction and associated technologies to extract and commercially produce high-purity lithium compounds from geothermal brine.  TerraLithium, a wholly owned subsidiary of Occidental, has patented DLE technologies that have the potential to process any lithium-containing brine into a responsibly sourced supply of high-purity lithium.
Commercial Plans: Processing Done by the Same Lead Developer/Parent Company: Originally the plan was to process onsite to lithium hydroxide, but the developer switched to lithium carbonate; easier to process but hydroxide is prefered by some EV battery manufacturers. 
Financial Support: Federal Agency: This grant was rescinded when the developer decided not to pursue the terms of the award.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: State: Contingent support of Lithium Valley Commission, recognizing need to manage risks. California Governor Newsome and Congressman Paul Ruiz support the Project. In 2022, California passed a law imposing new taxes on companies engaged in lithium extraction at the Salton Sea. The legislation designates 80% of the generated tax revenue to be distributed among the counties near these plants, with the remaining 20% allocated for the restoration of the Salton Sea. The law has the potential to bring millions in revenue to the historically underfunded region.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Federal: President Biden's domestic-policy advisor Gina McCarthy visited the Salton Sea to endorse the projects.  President Biden himself praised the Salton Sea Projects as a strategy to reduce US dependence on China for processed lithium. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Cahuilla Indian Reservation; Fort Yuma Quechan Tribe. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Earthworks
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: Poses risks to both water quality and quantity due to reliance on already struggling aquifers

Location: Additional Location Information: The project’s plants and facilities will be located on undeveloped land owned by the Imperial Irrigation District, which is about 3.6 miles southwest of Niland on 16 parcels. The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties at the southern end of California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico.
Project Description: Mining Method: Direct lithium extraction- ion-exchange technology.  
Project Description: Status of Project: The project is fully permitted and in January 2024 the developer broke ground on a commercial-scale facility to produce both renewable power and lithium hydroxide. 
Developer Description: Lead Developer: Controlled Thermal Resources Holdings, Inc. (CTR) is a U.S. company specializing in lithium and battery material products and renewable energy with projects in advanced development in the United States.  The company, which redomiciled to the United States in 2022, was established in 2013 and has headquarters in Imperial County, California. Additional offices are located in Brisbane, Australia, and in Houston, Texas. 
Financial Support: Public Supply Agreement w/ an Automaker or Battery/Component Producer: The developer has offtake agreements with General Motors, Stellantis and Statevolt (US battery manufacturer). 
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: Imperial County Board of Supervisors. 
Statements of Support from Public Officials: State: Contingent support of Lithium Valley Commission, recognizing need to manage risks. California Governor Newsome and Congressman Paul Ruiz support the Project. In 2022, California passed a law imposing new taxes on companies engaged in lithium extraction at the Salton Sea. The legislation designates 80% of the generated tax revenue to be distributed among the counties near these plants, with the remaining 20% allocated for the restoration of the Salton Sea. The law has the potential to bring millions in revenue to the historically underfunded region.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Federal: President Biden's domestic-policy advisor Gina McCarthy visited the Salton Sea to endorse the projects. President Biden himself praised the Salton Sea Projects as a strategy to reduce US dependence on China for processed lithium. 
Litigation: Court Rulings Issued: A California Superior Court judge (lowest level) has ruled against environmental and tribal groups, allowing the CTR DLE project at the Salton Sea to proceed. The judge ruled that the County did analyze the environmental impacts and did reach out to the tribes for their views.
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Cahuilla Indian Reservation; Fort Yuma Quechan Tribe. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Earthworks
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: Poses risks to both water quality and quantity due to reliance on already struggling aquifers
Reasons for Support: Economic Growth: According to an economist contracted by the County, the new facility will employ 250 construction workers for two-year stretches during the building phase, and 75 full-time operational jobs at the plant. He says that over a 30-year period the project will have a $1.6 billion impact on the regional economy.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 38 miles south of Darby (pop 780, 2020) near the headwaters of the Bitterroot River in the Bitterroot National Forest (south of the Painted Rocks Reservoir), southwest Montana.
Project Description: Existing Mine: Commercial mining hasn’t taken place in the Bitterroot National Forest for decades. Previous mining activity in the Forest includes the Skalkaho Vermiculite Deposit in the Sapphire Mountains east of Hamilton, but mining hasn’t taken place for decades. The most recent activity was an EIS (environmental impact statement) approved in 1993, but the mine never went into operation and the disturbance has since been reclaimed.
Project Description: Status of Project: The developer’s original plan was to submit in 2024 a plan of operations to the USFS that includes exploratory drilling.  However, the developer decided to delay that submission until 2025 as it consults with nearby communities and completes low-disturbance soil and rock sampling.
Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?: In 2024 the Canadian-based company U.S. Critical Metals pulled out of the project but retains a 12% stake in U.S. Critical Materials.
Financial Support: Federal Agency: Small amounts of DOE and DOD R&D funding.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: Contiguous footprint of over 218 federal lode mining claims over approximately 4,503 acres plus an Arizona state exploration permit for 640 acres.
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Center for Biological Diversity; Local/Regional -- Friends of the Bitterroot, Alliance for the Wild Rockies, Friends of the Clearwater, and the Montana Environmental Information Center
Concerned Interest Groups: Recreational Groups: Trout Unlimited (TU) and Backcountry Hunters & Anglers (BHA)
Reasons for Concern: Classification of Species Impacted: There are concerns about the possible impacts of the Project on wolverines (threatened), bull trout, Canada lynx, mountain goats, Northern Rockies fisher and grizzly bears. 
Reasons for Concern: Inadequate Community Engagement: The groups contend that USFS and the developer have not engaged adequately with the public.
Reasons for Concern: Other: Possible asbestos exposure; concern that the stable, thriving economy in the area might be replaced with boom/bust cycle

Location: Additional Location Information: Located southwest of Tucson and west of the near towns of Green Valley (pop 22,616, 2020) and Sahuarita (pop 34,134, 2020), close to the Mexican border. 
Project Description: Existing Mine: Started as underground mine in 1920s, then open pit method in 1945.
Project Description: Status of Project: Serrita is the third largest copper-producing mine in the US and has sufficient reserves to be operated past 2090. Project has 873.6 million tonnes of ore grading 0.36% copper. 
Was There a Change in Ownership during Project?: Claimed in 1882 and changed hands several times before FCX acquired it. Current developer acquired it in 2007.
Processing Plan: Processing Done by the Same Lead Developer/Parent Company: Some processing occurs on site.  Looking forward, SX/EW plant will produce approximately 9 million pounds per year of copper cathode from solution generated by low-grade stockpile leaching.
A pressure-leach plant will process molybdenum concentrate.  
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: City council members
Reasons for Concern: Traffic & Noise: Nearby town of Kirkland resistant to mine expansion, don't want exacerbated traffic & noise.
Reasons for Concern: Air Quality: The developer has had a persistent challenge in controlling dust emissions from the tailings pile, though progress has been made in recent years with advanced dust suppression techniques.
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: Some ecologists fear that the land sale will lead to species habitat loss and water-quality issues.
Reasons for Support: Employment: 1080 direct jobs, 3,970 total jobs in the state of Arizona.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located next to the Ironwood Forest National Monument near Mirana (pop 51,906, 2020), 36 miles northwest of Tucson, Arizona.  Silver Bell is an abandoned mining town that existed twice. The project site is 4 miles southeast of the original town site.
Project Description: Mining Method: Shift from underground to surface mining occurred after World War 2.
Project Description: Status of Project: A major expansion of the mine is unlikely. More copper resources may exist east and west of the currently active mining area, but that ground is effectively off-limits because it lies within Ironwood Forest National Monument.
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: Silver Bell is an active mine with expansion potential east and west of the current footprint. However, that ground is off-limits because it lies within the Ironwood Forest National Monument. Congress has generally placed land around National Monuments off limits to mining.
Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?: ASARCO acquired the site in 1915.  Sold 25% interest to Mitsui in 1996.  Resumed 100% ownership in 2014. ASARCO owned by Grupo Mexico, largest mining company in Mexico.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Commercial Plans: Processing Done by the Same Lead Developer/Parent Company: Copper-bearing solutions from the dump leach and rubble areas are collected and pumped to the solvent extraction plant where the copper in solution is concentrated over 30 times before being pumped to the tank house. In the tank house, the copper is recovered from solution using the electrowinning process and plated on stainless steel starter sheets as high-purity cathodes.  Cathode copper produced in the solvent extraction / electrowinning (SX/EW) operation is sold to producers of copper rod, tubing and wire.
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: ASARCO will pay $170,000 in civil penalties for dumping 340,000 gallons of wastewater containing sulfuric acid and heavy metal into dry washes on three different occasions. 
Reasons for Concern: Classification of Species Impacted: Threatened jaguar. 
Reasons for Concern: Reputation of the Developer/Parent Company: Critics point to Mexican parent company of developer as company with reputation for “union busting” and toxic spills. 
Reasons for Support: Other: Generation of specialized copper products for industry

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 40 miles southwest of Tonopah (pop 2,179, 2020), near town of Silver Peak (pop 213, 2022), Clayton Valley, western edge of Nevada near the California line. 
Project Description: Status of Project: The developer was doubling production at Silver Peak when the global lithium slump caused financial problems (2023-2024) for the developer.  It is not yet clear whether the expansion will be delayed or pared back.  
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: While Albemarle was initially granted all the water rights in the county, with more lithium companies beginning operations in the area, they have had to defend their water rights in judicial and regulatory proceedings.
Commercial Plans: Processing Dome by the Same Lead Developer/Parent Company: Onsite chemical processing makes it into lithium carbonate; a small lithium hydroxide conversion plant operates on site. Some of the carbonate from Silver Peak is sent to Albemarle’s processing facility in Kings Mountain, North Carolina. There it can be further refined into lithium hydroxide, which is used for electric vehicle batteries.  First stage processing: brine is taken to an on-site plant, where lime and soda ash is added to further the transformation; it is then filtered, pressed and dried into lithium carbonate. 
Commercial Plans: Total Capital Costs: $30-50 million for expansion project 
Financial Support: Federal Agency: $9.3 million of a $30 million DOE grant (2024) to Albemarle will be used to support expansion of lithium carbonate production at Silver Peak. 
Land Ownership: Type of Land: Public and Private: 6,068 acres is private land owned by – or leased to – Albemarle; another 1,318 acres is on public land administered by the BLM.  
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: There is a long history of litigation over water rights in water-stressed Clayton Valley, Nevada as Albemarle claims almost exclusive access (as it operates the Silver Peak lithium mine and has expansion plans).  Other developers have sued Albemarle seeking access, claiming that Albemarle is not using all of its allotted water rights and they don't last forever.  One developer, Nevada Sunrise, was in litigation with Albemarle from 2017-2019 and finally reached a settlement in July 2019.    
Reasons for Concern: Impacts to Natural Environment: Concern of land consumption
Reasons for Concern: Other: Concern that economy will enter a boom/bust cycle

Project Name: Also called Phase 1A Project. The LANXESS Project refers to a suite of contemplated staged expansion projects relating to the LANXESS South, Central, and West Brine Production Units. This Commercial Lithium Extraction Plant Project at
LANXESS South Plant (Phase 1A or Project) is the first stage of development of the LANXESS Project.
Location: Additional Location Information: Located 8 miles southwest of El Dorado, a city in and the county seat of Union County, on the southern border of Arkansas. The Smackover Formation is a limestone aquifer that spans across several states in the southern United States, including Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama. It includes a broad area of oil and gas production and a region of active production of bromine. While the area is now mostly emptied of fossil fuels, it is filled with a brine that contains lithium, perhaps the highest lithium concentrations in continental brines in the United States. 
Project Description: Mining Method: The developer has selected the Lithium Selective Sorption (LSS) process as the Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) process for the project. LSS is a Koch Technology Solutions, LLC (KTS) proprietary technology to extract lithium ions from pre-treated Smackover brine.
Project Description: Status of Project: This brownfield development aims to achieve significant commercial lithium production by processing tail brine from the existing bromine operations at the LANXESS South Plant in Union County, Arkansas. The developer commissioned a demonstration plant at LANXESS’ South Plant facility in May 2020 and the LSS DLE process has been in operation at the Demonstration plant since October 2022.The future plan features a commercial-scale Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) and lithium carbonate conversion facility by 2026. The feasibility study was completed in 2023.  
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: The developer is looking into constructing a facility to process Li into Lithium Carbonate at the El Dorado facility.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: LANXESS, a specialty chemicals company, has exclusive brine extraction rights for 149,442 acres which is contained within three brine production units, known as the South, Central, and West Brine Units.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: Mayor of Magnolia supports the project.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located approximately 15 miles west of the City of Magnolia in Lafayette County, southwestern Arkansas, United States. The SWA Property lies wholly within Lafayette and Columbia counties. The Smackover Formation is a limestone aquifer that spans across several states in the southern United States, including Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama. It includes a broad area of oil and gas production and a region of active production of bromine. While the area is now mostly emptied of fossil fuels, it is filled with a brine that contains lithium, perhaps the highest lithium concentrations in continental brines in the United States.  
Project Description: Mining Method: The developer will use conventional oil and gas drilling methods to access lithium-rich saltwater from reservoirs about 10,000 ft underground, and then apply direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology to separate lithium from the saltwater.  The remaining saltwater will be reinjected into the underground reservoirs. 
Project Description: Status of Project: The developer plans to begin production in 2027.  Development may be slowed by the State of Arkansas's slow pace in resolving the size of royalties.  
Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?: The developer acquired its Smackover rights from Galvanic Energy in early 2023. Building on the deal with Galvanic, the developer entered into a partnership with Tetra Technologies Inc. to jointly develop 6,100 lithium-rich Smackover formation acres.
Commercial Plans: Processing Done by the Same Lead Developer/Parent Company: Once lithium is extracted from brine, the developer will convert it onsite to battery-grade material.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: The SWA Property is comprised of 489 land tracts containing 851 individual leases and eight salt water (brine) deeds that covers 27,066 net mineral acres (10,953 net mineral hectares). The proposed unitized SWA Property encompasses 36,839 gross mineral acres (14,908 gross mineral hectares) and forms the updated 2023 resource and project area. The leases and deeds are held by TETRA. TETRA began acquiring brine deeds and/or brine leases in 1992 and added additional brine leases in 1994, 2006 and 2017. Standard Lithium acquired the SWA Project brine production rights to lithium directly from TETRA through an option agreement providing that Standard Lithium makes annual payments.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: The Magnolia Mayor announced support for further development of the Smackover Formation, including bromine and lithium.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: State: State Rep. Wade Andrews, R-Camden, indicated support for lithium plans due to the economic development stimulus in the impoverished area.
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Earthworks
Reasons For Concern: Water Quality: Brines can contain naturally-occurring toxic substances plus those from previous drilling operations. 
Reasons for Concern: Other: Inadequate royalties. 
Reasons for Support: Cleaner than Other Sources: Cleaner if mined here rather than if mined abroad.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 20 miles north of the Mexican border, 7 miles from the town of Patagonia (pop 804, 2020), 15.5 miles northeast of the Town of Nogales (pop 19,770, 2020) in southern Arizona; about 50 miles south of Tucson in the in southern Patagonia mountains. 
Project Description: Status of Project: The developer’s 2024 diamond core drilling program revealed high-grade copper-silver and lead-zinc-silver veins, underscoring the promise of the project.
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: A previous developer was awarded a permit by USFS for exploratory drilling but, in 2015, environmental groups persuaded a district court that USFS had not performed an adequate NEPA analysis.  Further delays occurred when the previous developer and another developer disputed land rights around the project.  The current developer again obtained a USFS permit for exploratory drilling and, in 2023-2024, worked with the USFS to defeat another lawsuit against USFS, which called for a preliminary injunction against the exploration permit based on environmental concerns. A key theme of this lawsuit is that USFS allegedly failed to consider the cumulative harm from multiple mining projects in the same mountainous ecosystem.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?:The developer acquired 100% ownership of the project from Ragsdale in May 2021.  Previously it was a joint venture.                                                                                                                                                                                  
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: In the first case, environmental groups persuaded a federal district court (2015) to block an exploratory drilling plan until the USFS and the developer completed an adequate environmental analysis (EA). The USFS had granted the developer a categorical exclusion for an EA under NEPA because of the limited duration and scope of the exploration plan.   In the second case, environmentalists in 2023 sought a preliminary injunction against exploratory drilling at the site.  A federal district court and the 9th Circuit refused to grant the injunction; the merits of the lawsuit are being heard in the federal district court in 2024.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local -- Patagonia Area Resource Alliance (PARA); National -- Defenders of Wildlife
Reason for Concern: Classification of Species Impacted: Concerns have been expressed about endangered species such as the jaguar and ocelot, and threatened species such as the Mexican spotted owl and the Western yellow-billed cuckoos.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 1.5 miles north of Tamarack (pop 57, 2020), 10 miles east of McGregor (pop 384, 2020), and 30 miles west of Cloquet (pop 12,568, 2020) in central Minnesota; around 130 miles north of Minneapolis and 50 miles west of Duluth.
Project Description: Status of Project: Talon’s proposed nickel-copper-cobalt mine is currently being submitted for federal environmental review. Once approved, it could potentially enter production as soon as 2028.    
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: In 2024, the developer submitted its seventh exploration plan, seeking agency approval. Concerns have been raised by both tribal and environmental groups. 
Developer Description: Lead Developer: The project is being developed through a joint venture with Kennecott, a subsidiary of Rio Tinto.
Developer Description: Parent Company: Talon Metals owns 51% of the Tamarack project. The other 49% is owned by Kennecott- Exploration Company, a subsidiary of Rio Tinto.
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: Processing will occur in a nearby town in North Dakota. 
Financial Support: Federal Agency: DOE $114 million grant for a processing plant in nearby North Dakota. Talon has also been awarded $21 M from DOD, some which may be used at Tamarack. In 2024, the US Department of Defense awarded Talon a $2.4 million contract to aid research and development into new techniques for extracting minerals from nickel sulphide ores and tailings. The research will focus on the Tamarack project. 
Financial Support: Public Supply Agreement w/ Automaker or Battery/Component Producer: Talon has an agreement with Tesla Inc. to supply 75,000 metric tonnes (165 million lbs) of nickel in concentrate (and certain by-products, including cobalt and iron) from the Tamarack Nickel Project over an estimated six-year period.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: 90% state owned lands, 10% private land.
Litigation: Court Rulings Issued: In early stages of environmental review but may face obstacles similar toTwin Metals. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe, Tribe of the Lake Superior Chippewa, Ojibwe tribe
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local -- Tamarack Water Alliance
Reasons for Concern: Land Use (Built Environment): Concern of increased traffic and disruptions from heavy trucks and rail routes.
Reasons for Concern: Impacts to Natural Environment: Concern about possible permanent ecological damage to surrounding wetlands and forests.
Reasons for Concern: Site of Historical, Cultural, Spiritual Significance: Risk of disruption to tribal way of life; Fear dust from mine will hurt manoomin (a wild rice crucial to tribal diet); Also fear disruption of subsistence hunting, fishing, and harvesting of plants.
Reasons for Concern: Traffic & Noise: Increased truck traffic and noise from explosions.
Reasons for Concern: Air Quality: Concerns about air pollution from mine vents and mineral dust.
Reasons for Concern: Water Supply: Risk of mining-related activities affecting local aquifers and water availability.
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: Fear of sulfuric acid drainage polluting lakes and rivers; Potential rise in sulfate levels harming water quality and aquatic ecosystems; Risk of toxic heavy metals leaching into groundwater.
Reasons for Concern: Impact on Species: Potential harm to plant and animal species reliant on clean water, such as wild rice.
Reasons for Concern: Recreation: Risk of disruption to tourists and seasonal residents
Reasons for Concern: Agriculture: Risk to tree farms and agricultural areas from land use changes.
Reasons for Concern: Subsistence Hunting/Fishing: Threat to tribal subsistence fishing and hunting practices due to pollution and ecosystem disruption.
Reasons for Concern: Historical Mining or Reclamation Issues: Allegedly empty reclamation promises in previous mining projects
Reasons for Concern: Reputation of the Developer/Parent Company: Distrust of Rio Tinto due to prior controversies, including destruction of cultural heritage sites; Doubts about Talon’s environmental claims and "Green Nickel" branding.
Reasons for Concern: Inadequate Community Engagement: Perception of insufficient consultation with Indigenous tribes and local communities; Concerns about a lack of transparency in the environmental review and approval process.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 21 miles west-northwest of Orovada (pop 117, 2020) and 60 miles north-northwest of Winnemucca (pop 8,431, 2020) within the McDermitt Caldera (an old volcanic complex on the Nevada-Oregon border); 200 miles north of Reno in northwest Nevada.
Project Description: Status of Project: The fully permitted project is now under construction, with full production scheduled for 2028.
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: The project was delayed several years due to permitting delays and lawsuits related to the concerns of ranchers, environmentalists and tribal groups.  Regulatory deliberations may not have ended: The USFS has initiated a one-year study of an endangered snail at the project site. 
Financial Support: Federal Agency: DOE loan in final stages: $2.62 billion for lithium carbonate processing facility.
Financial Support: Public Supply Agreement w/ an Automaker or Battery/Component Producer: GM has restructured and expanded financial commitment to Thacker Pass. GM will invest $625 million in Thacker Pass (a 38% stake), Lithium America’s retains majority (62% stake). GM’s original plan was to invest only $328 million in the first phase.  GM receives exclusive rights to output from mine for first 20 years, then 38% of mine’s output in second 20 years.  
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Federal: Both the Trump administration (first term) and the Biden administration supported the project.
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: There were two lawsuits against BLM's decision about Thacker Pass in the same federal court. The first one focused on the environmental impacts and was led by a rancher, environmental groups, and two tribes. The second brought in additional tribes and focused on whether BLM engaged in proper consultation with the tribes. The plaintiffs lost the original lawsuit  in both the district court and the 9th Circuit. The second one lost in district court and the tribes decided not to appeal to the 9th Circuit. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Reno-Sparks Indian Colony, Burns Paiute Tribe, and Summit Lake Paiute Tribe.
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Center for Biological Diversity; Local/Regional -- Western Watersheds Project, Wildlands Defense, Great Basin Resource Watch, and Basin and Range Watch.
Concern Groups: Evidence of Organized Protests: At least three instances of barricade and protests camps. 
Reasons for Concern: Site of Historical, Cultural, Spiritual Significance: Where US Cavalry allegedly massacred the Paiute people.
Reasons for Concern: Impact on Species: Rare Kings River pyrg, a tiny aquatic snail; additional listed species such as the sage grouse, Lahontan cutthroat trout, old growth sagebrush.
Reasons for Concern: Reputation of the Developer/Parent Company: Critics point to the developer's alleged human rights violations in Argentina.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 6 miles northwest of Tonopah (pop 2,179, 2020) in the Big Smoky Valley, halfway between Reno and Las Vegas. 
Project Description: Status of Project:  Exploration -- The 2024 drilling program will allow an update to the January 2023 resource estimate.  Environmental baseline study work and hydrology/water monitoring are on-going as the developer readies to commence the Mine Plan of Operations permitting process.
Reasons for Support: Cleaner than Other Sites: Some lithium projects pose much less ecological risk than others due to absence of nearby groundwater-dependent ecosystems and absence of habitat for endangered and threatened species.  Projects around Tonopah may be especially low in ecological risk, TLC and Tonopah Flats have been mentioned specifically.

Location: Additional Location Information: Approximately 25-30 miles south of Casa Grande, near the village of North Komelik, Pinal County, southwestern Arizona.                                         Land Ownership: Type of Land: Private land -- Developer has 4,180 acres of land leased from the Bureau of Indian Affairs and the Tohono O’odham Nation.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located in Big Smoky Valley 5 miles west of town of Tonopah (2179, 2020) between the San Antonio Mountains to the east and the Monte Cristo Mountains to the west. Tonopah is located at the junction of U.S. Routes 6 and 95, approximately midway between Las Vegas and Reno, Nevada.
Project Description: Existing Mine: Production ended in 1982, peak production in 1953.
Project Description: Status of Project: Exploration. 2023 drilling program led to updated mineral resource estimates in a 2024 technical report.  Since Tonopah Flats is an unconventional claystone resource, the developer has advanced first-of-kind lithium hydroxide extraction and purification processes specific to the site’s claystone material.  In 2024 the developer finished construction of an integrated pilot scale facility to demonstrate these processes.
Financial Support: Federal Agency: The developer has received a DOE grant to help finance a commercial scale lithium hydroxide refinery, a DOE grant for a demonstration facility of techniques to convert claystone into lithium hydroxide, and multiple DOE tax credits for battery recycling facilities. 
Reasons for Support: Cleaner than Other Sources: Some lithium projects pose much less ecological risk than others due to absence of nearby groundwater-dependent ecosystems and absence of habitat for endangered and threatened species.  Projects around Tonopah may be especially low in ecological risk, TLC and Tonopah Flats have been mentioned specifically.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located approximately 10 miles southwest of Salmon, Lemhi County, Idaho with a population of 6,724.              Project Descriprtion: Status of Project: The developer plans a 2500m drill program to test the extensions of  high grade surface zones at depth.  In September 2022 USFS approved drilling 30 holes averaging 1,000 on 10 drilling pads along Torney Creek and Perreau Creek.                                                                                                                                                                                          Land Ownership: Type of Land: Salmon-Challis Forest

Location: Additional Location Information: Located 9 miles southeast of Ely (3,268, 2020) and 11 miles northeast of Babbitt (pop 1,397, 2020) in northeastern Minnesota. The site is part of the  Duluth Complex geologic formation and is located near the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness.
Project Description: Status of Project: Under the Biden administration, the developer’s leases were canceled and a 20-year moratorium was placed on underground mining in the Superior National Forest. Recently (late 2023), the developer obtained permission from the state to explore on nearby state-owned land not covered by the federal moratorium. 
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: The Obama, Trump and Biden administrations flip flopped on the validity of the developer’s leases, which were invalid as of December 2024.  The developer was unsuccessful in the first round of litigation (2022) aimed at restoring the leases; in November 2023 the developer appealed that decision to the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals. The DC Circuit may not reach a verdict, since the Department of Justice under President Trump may request that the Trump administration be given an opportunity to resolve the issue.  President Trump has pledged to allow the project to move forward, but a complex bureaucratic process is required to make that happen.
Developer Description: Parent Company: A local Duluth-based company explored the site and then partnered with a Chilean-based multinational to help finance and develop it.  The two companies formed Twin Metals Inc, the current developer.
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan Elsewhere in North America: The developer has no on-site processing plan but processing could occur at facilities in Canada and/or Mexico.
Statements of Concern from Public Officials: Local: Since 2016, the nearby community of Ely has been divided on the merits of the project, with intense views on both sides. 
Litigation: Evidence of Litigation: The first case addressed whether the Trump administration (2017), through BLM, was allowed to reinstate the leases for Twin Metals that the Obama administration had cancelled (2016). A federal district court ruled that the leases were reinstated lawfully.  When the Biden Administration, through BLM and USFS, rescinded the leases again, and the developer sued, a federal district court (2023) ruled that the rescissions were lawful. The developer sued to regain the leases but lost its suit in federal district court. The developer appealed to the DC Circuit Court of Appeals, which was deliberating in 2024.
Concerned Interest Groups: Indigenous Groups: Ojibwe and Chippewa Tribes 
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local/Regional -- Friends of the Boundary Waters Wilderness; National -- Earthjustice, Wilderness Society, Izaak Walton League of America
Reasons for Concern: Impacts to Natural Environment: Project is located near the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness and Superior National Forest, raising concerns about potential environmental degradation and threats to waters and ecosystems.
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: surface and groundwater quality concerns.
Reasons for Concern: Recreation: Concern over impact on tourism.
Reasons for Concern: Historical Mining or Reclamation Issues: History of pollution from other mines in area, including inadequate reclamation.
Reasons for Concern: Reputation of the Developer/Parent Company: Critics of the project point to the fact that the Chilean parent company has been accused of various wrong doings in its home country of Chile.
Reasons for Support: Other: Supportive of better labor standards than mines abroad

Location: Additional Location Information: Closest towns are Moab (pop 5,366, 2020), Grand County, southeastern Utah and Grand Junction, western Colorado. (Located in Paradox Basin:  Intreprid Potash’s Cane Creek potash mine is 32 miles to the northwest; Anson’s lithium project is 38 miles to the northwest).                                                                          Project Description: Status of Project: The developer has already compiled detailed datasets relating to historic well logs, petrophysics, stratigraphy and local geology, Going forward, the developer will conduct exploration work toward the upgrade of the Mineral Resource from Inferred to Indicated in accordance with JORC 2012; sample existing wells (and potential drilling of new well(s)) to obtain brine to verify historical lithium-brine geochemical results; conduct initial mineral processing test work to validate the potential extraction of lithium from Paradox Basin brine; and identify the reservoirs and/or areas with the greatest lithium-brine potential.                                                                                                                                                            Project Description: Change in Ownership: The developer confirmed partial acquisition of the Utah lithium project in May 2023, securing over 80,000 acres prospective for lithium brines in the Paradox Basin. It now fully owns 93,755 acres, or 379 square kilometres.                                                                                                                                         Commericial Plans: Processing Plan in US: Plan for two pilot DLE processing facilities.  Two DLE partners have produced battery-grade Lithium
Hydroxide directly from Mandrake brine. DLE developer, Electroflow Technologies, achieved 92% conversion to lithium hydroxide with no chemical pretreatment of brine.    Rio-Tinto-backed ElectraLith successfully produced 99.9% pure battery-grade Lithium Hydroxide from Mandrake’s brines.                                                                                                      Finacial Support: Federal Agency: US$1 Million grant awarded by US Department of Energy (DOE) to a consortium of Mandrake, Idaho National Laboratories (INL), National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) and University of Utah.  Will give Mandrake access to the foremost U.S.
scientists and sophisticated U.S.-funded laboratories, plus cash to part fund forthcoming re-entry activities at oil and gas well sites.  Additional DOE applications for further funding are in process.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located in the western region of the Upper Peninsula, Michigan, near the small communities White Pine (pop 339, 2020), Ontonagon (pop 1,285, 2020), Bergland (pop 141, 2020), Wakefield (pop 1,702, 2020), and Ironwood (pop 5,045, 2020).
Project Description: Existing Mine: White Pine Mine is an abandoned site, in 1952 constructed by Copper Range.
Project Description: Status of Project: In 2024 the developer initiated a second drill program of approximately 14,500 metres to collect samples for engineering study test work, in addition to assaying for the purposes of a resource update.  Key engineering trade-off studies and environmental baselining were also initiated to support permit requests.
Developer Description: Was There Change in Ownership during Project?: Highland Copper Company Inc. formed a joint venture with Kinterra Copper LLC in July 2023.
Statements of Support from Public Officials: Local: The project has received resolutions of support from all townships within Gogebic County and multiple neighboring communities (i.e., the city councils of local municipalities).
Statements of Support from Public Officials: State: Governor of Michigan 
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: National -- Sierra Club (Wisconsin Chapter); Local/Regional -- Mining Action Group
Reason for Concern: Impacts to Natural Environment: Fears of mining impacts from pollution (e.g., airborne pollutants, soils and waters contaminated with heavy metals) that may degrade the natural habitat of the Porcupine Mountains, especially the Presque Isle Scenic Area and the Presque Isle Rustic Campground. 
Reasons for Concern: Historical Mining or Reclamation Issues: Legacy contamination concerns. The site included an ore-refining smelter with a 500′ tall stack; new research shows that mercury emissions from White Pine Smelter contaminated a wide swath of the Upper Peninsula. EPA will expect the developer to engage in remediation activity as part of the project.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located in the Alvord Desert in southeast Oregon near the town of Fields (pop 120, 2020); across the border in Nevada is the Lithium Americas’ Thacker Pass lithium project.
Location: Mineral Occurrence: The developer’s attempted claims were located on a volcanic field to the north of the McDermott and Thacker Pass lithium projects near the Nevada line.  The developer became intrigued due to some 1970s USGS sampling of two springs at nearby private land. 
Project Description: Status of Project: Without an amendment to section 401 of the Steens Cooperative Management and Protection Act of 2000, the project will not be able to proceed.  In 2000 Congress withdrew from development a large swatch of land in eastern Oregon that includes the Steed Mountains, including the Alvord Desert.
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: The BLM determined in 2022 that the land staked by the developer was placed off limits to mining by a conservation law (the Steens Act) passed at the end of the Clinton administration (2000).
Developer Description: Parent Company: ACME Lithium Inc. is developing two sites in southwest Nevada and two in Manitoba, Canada.
Land Ownership: Year of Land Acquisition: Company staked 340 placer mining claims encompassing approx. 6727 acres near the Nevada border in southeast Oregon in late March 2022
Concerned Interest Groups: Community Residents/Groups: Local landowners brought the land stakes to the attention of BLM.

Location: Additional Location Information: Located in southeast Arizona near the town of Wilcox (3,213 pop, 2020) and the Cochise Stronghold, a beautiful woodland area;  200 miles southeast of Phoenix. 
Project Description: Mining Method: Undetermined: Developer is researching pretreatment, concentration, extraction, purification and post-treatment of lithium to develop new extraction technologies for brine resources.
Project Description: Status of Project: In 2023-2024, the developer demonstrated through first-ever diamond drilling and clay separation that the Playa may host a top-tier lithium deposit extending from the developer’s ground through claims leased by the Defense Department. The developer’s BLM claims to the south may provide some of the most compelling targets on the property, and are a priority in the next phase of drilling.
Land Ownership: Type of Land: The developer acquired 3,754 acres, mostly leased from the state of Arizona. Southern claims are BLM land.
Statements of Concern from Public Officials: Local: Some local residents fear impacts on the Sandhill Cranes, which thousands of tourists come to see each year. 
Concerned Interest Groups: Community Residents/Groups: In 2023 a community group named “Help Save the Willcox Playa” began to coagulate online with the mission of slowing or stopping the proposed mine. Group plans to join with large environmental groups.
Concerned Interest Groups: Scale of Environmental Groups: Local -- Help Save the Wilcox Playa.
Reasons for Concern: Water Supply: The Wilcox basin is undergoing a water crisis. The valley’s water table, fed entirely by rainfall, has seen a dramatic decrease in levels over time, drying up wells for farmers, ranchers and homesteads. Fears are that a mine with water evaporation as an extraction mechanism will further deplete the water table. Also, mine is adjacent to the aquifer that supplies groundwater to the northern parts of Cochise County.
Reasons for Concern: Water Quality: Some residents fear contamination of water, soil and air in an area known for its sweeping winds and a thriving wildlife corridor. They say winds could track pollutants all over the valley, injuring all habitats. Also, the mine is adjacent to the aquifer that supplies groundwater to the northern parts of Cochise County.
Reasons for Concern: Impact on Species: Special concern about any threat to the Sandhill Crane.
Reasons for Concern: Recreation: Concerned about potential impact on tourism, thousands travel to see the Sandhill Cranes each year,

Project Name: Yerington and MacArthur properties, which are part of the Company's Yerington Copper Project.
Location: Additional Location Information: Near Yerington (3,048, 2020) and Weed Heights, Lyon County,  Nevada, Mason Valley, about 70 miles southeast of Reno.
Project Description: Mining Method: The PEA indicates that the Yerington Copper Project holds potential for phased open pit mining. These pits would feed sulfide material to a dedicated Nuton™ (Nuton) Heap Leach Facility (HLF) equipped with a 17 Mtpa crushing and agglomerating system that employs conveyors for material stacking on the HLF. Additionally, oxide material would be placed on a separate HLF near the sulfide facility, involving run-of-mine (ROM) oxide from Yerington and the residuals composed of the W-3 and VLT stockpiles. Oxide material from MacArthur would undergo sizing, conveying, agglomeration and then stacking on the oxide HLF, facilitated by a 25 Mtpa system.  Nuton technologies comprise a proprietary suite of Rio Tinto-developed copper heap leaching technologies aimed to recover primary copper sulfides. Copper recoveries from Yerington sulfide materials demonstrate an increase from below 25% to 74% for the sample tests to date, with an acid consumption calculated at 32 lb/ton. At this point in time (January 2024), the testing of Nuton technology on Yerington sulfide materials is ongoing. Preliminary results are promising. 
Project Description: Status of Project:  The objective of the 2024 Yerington drilling program was to convert as much of the inferred resource as possible to the indicated resource classification so that it can be included in the prefeasibility study ("PFS"). The recently concluded drilling, together with the discovery of an additional 17 historic Anaconda holes that were not included in the January 2024 Preliminary Economic Assessment ("PEA"), are now being incorporated into an updated mineral resource as a key input into the PFS now in process.
Commercial Plans: Processing Plan in US: According to Lion Copper, the leaching process using Nuton’s methods can deliver recovery rates of 74% and eliminate the need for a concentrator, tailings impoundment, and resource-intense smelter operations.  The SXEW facilities will be located near the Nuton HLF. This technology is well-established and has a proven track record in industrial applications, resulting in the production of LME Grade A copper cathode using accepted industry reagents. The engineering and design of the SXEW facility is modular in nature, enabling shorter construction timelines and the flexibility to expand as necessary during the ramp- up phase. The initial SXEW production capacity is set at 70 million pounds per annum of copper cathode, with the capability to increase to 140 million pounds per annum through the addition of supplementary SXEW modules.

Location: Additional Location Information: Halfway between Vegas and Reno, 220 miles southeast of Reno, accessed via Silver Peak, which is 7 miles west or from Tonopah, NV (pop 2,179, 2020), which is located 27 miles northeast; Esmeralda County, Nevada; perimeter of Zeus is as close as 1 mile from Albemarle’s Silver Peak. 
Project Description: Mining Method: It is recommended that mining methods be developed for the Zeus mineralized material, including an evaluation of use of coal-seam style scrapers to minimize mining costs. A mine schedule for the high-grade core of the deposit should be developed as the basis for the PEA mine plan. All of the lithium mineralization is hosted within clays hosted by the Esmeralda Formation.
Project Description: Status of Project: The developer has completed a total of 92 drillholes in seven phases of drilling between 2017 to 2024. The updated 2023-2024 Mineral Resource statement for the Zeus project includes the addition of 10 drillholes and their associated assay data from the Phase VII drilling program, comprehensive geological work including detailed geological mapping, review of historic drillholes and logs, review of literature regarding analogous deposits, the development of an ore deposit model and geological model to synthesize that work, and the collection of 167 density measurements as well as 32 tests of moisture content. 
Project Description: Regulatory Challenges: In early February 2024, the developer received notification from the state that the County of Esmeralda had filed a protest against the Company’s water rights applications. The developer is engaging with the County and its advisors to resolve the concerns.  
Developer Description: Lead Developer: The company was formerly known as Noram Ventures Inc. and changed its name to Noram Lithium Corp. in July 2021. The company was incorporated in 2010 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada
Processing Plan: Processing Done by the Same Lead Developer/Parent Company: Multi-step, on-site processing into LCE is planned.  
Land Ownership: Type of Land: Developer acquired rights to the area in 2016. 146 placer claims and 136 lode claims. The land package covers 1,133 hectares (2,800 acres).
